BOZ64 co-op: same Wi-Fi, VPN apps, and direct play
=====================================================

Starting a game (all ways below)
  Every player opens CO-OP MULTIPLAYER > LOCAL WI-FI, picks the same map and presses Continue.
  The first player to get there hosts; the others find that game and join it.

Same Wi-Fi or home network
  Nothing to set up.

Radmin VPN, Hamachi, ZeroTier (VPNs that act like a home network)
  Everyone joins the same VPN network, then plays as above. Nothing else to set up: the game looks for games on
  every network the device is on, VPNs included.
  Radmin VPN and Hamachi are PC only. ZeroTier also has a phone app; if a phone on ZeroTier doesn't find the game,
  put the other player's ZeroTier address in peers.txt (below).

Tailscale, WireGuard (VPNs that don't pass broadcasts)
  One player writes the other's address (Tailscale: their 100.x.x.x address or machine name) in peers.txt.
  Only one side needs it.

Over the internet without a VPN
  The host forwards UDP port 47710 and TCP port 47711 on their router to their device. The other players write the
  host's public IP in peers.txt.

peers.txt
  PC:    next to boz64.exe (the game writes an example file there the first time it starts).
  Phone: Android/data/com.activision.boz64/files/peers.txt. Copy it there from a PC over USB.
  One address per line. Lines starting with # are ignored.

Windows Firewall
  When Windows asks about boz64.exe, tick both "Private" and "Public" networks. VPN adapters such as Radmin VPN
  usually count as Public, so allowing only Private blocks VPN play.

If a game isn't found
  - Check that both devices can reach each other (for example, ping the other player's VPN address).
  - Only one copy of the game per device can use UDP port 47710. A second copy on the same PC still finds games,
    but others can't find a game it hosts unless they put this PC's address in peers.txt.
  - boz64.log (next to boz64.exe) lists, under "lan:", the networks searched and the games found.
